messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pagerduty: KV cache fragmentation alarm - high GPU memory churn and elevated 5xx rate on hosted inference pool gpu-r1. Threshold triggered at 2026-03-14T02:15:12Z.
Dana (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a bunch of ptx OOMs and allocator logs. routing to eng-sre.
Erin (sre): Yep, traces show continuous batching spiking token allocations; arena allocation churn increasing fragmentation. Top stack frames point at `continuous_batch::combine` and `kv::arena::alloc_slab`.
Frank (eng-ml): initial thought: recent batching heuristic change increased max_batch_size to 2048 for some routes — likely far above expected seq length distribution. That could blow up KV cache prefetching.
Carlos R.: grabbing heap histograms and CUDA malloc logs from nodes in pool gpu-r1.
Alice M.: Customer impact: several PLG customers showing 500s and timeouts on text-gen routes. Support already got one ticket from Acme Inc.
Bob S.: ETA on rollback of batching heuristic? can we hotfix config?
Frank (eng-ml): We can push a runtime override to reduce continuous_batch.max_tokens and disable aggressive prefix caching for the affected model. Suggested quick patch:
```
continuous_batch.max_tokens=512
continuous_batch.enable_prefix_cache=false
```
Carlos R.: applying override to pool gpu-r1 (rollout -> canary 10% then 100%).
Carlos R.: `redwoodctl config set --pool gpu-r1 continuous_batch.max_tokens=512 --env live && redwoodctl config set --pool gpu-r1 continuous_batch.enable_prefix_cache=false --env live`
IncidentBot: Deploy started by Carlos R. Canary on 3 hosts.
Dana (oncall): toggling evictions to aggressive to bound KV growth: `kv:set_eviction_policy evict_lru aggressive`.
Erin (sre): attaching heap dump snippet:
```
allocator: arena count=48
kv_cache: total_slots=2.4M used=2.38M free_frag=14.6%
pytorch_malloc retries=7, last_error=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```
Frank (eng-ml): If fragmentation doesn't improve, we should trigger on-host arena compaction. I have a small script to walk arenas and attempt coalescing.
Alice M.: Support update: notifying affected customers (Acme Inc, Beta Labs) with ETA 30m, offering to reroute traffic where possible.
Carlos R.: Canary looks good on first 10m — 5xx count down by ~70% on canaries. rolling to rest of pool.
Bob S.: any signs of allocator metadata corruption? logs show normal but high slab splitting rate.
Erin (sre): No corruption. This is fragmentation + high allocation churn. compaction should help but is heavier. prefer config change first.
Frank (eng-ml): I've prepared a small allocator tweak branch that increases base_slab_size and reduces splitting thresholds. If canary rollback does not hold, plan to roll this as 1. patch -> canary 2. monitor 3. roll.
Dana (oncall): After full rollout, latency back within SLOs, 5xx returned near baseline. Marking P1 -> mitigation. We'll keep bridge open for postmortem.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 2026-03-14T03:42:10Z — topology stabilized.
Erin (sre): Postmortem action items:
- revert max_batch_size change in next deploy (FRANK)
- add guard rails: max_batch_tokens limit per route (ENG-RUNTIME)
- add allocator compaction job to run when free_frag < 25% for >5m (SRE)
- add telemetry: slab_split_rate, arena_coalesces per host (OBSERVABILITY)
Frank (eng-ml): I'll open PR for allocator tweak but gate it behind perf tests.
Carlos R.: I'll push a backfill script to compute affected requests and notify product for potential refunds.
Alice M.: Support will send customer follow-up and root cause summary.
Bob S.: kudos to the team — quick triage and rollback. :thumbsup:
SupportBot: Notified customers: Acme Inc (ticket #12345), Beta Labs (ticket #12346).
Dana (oncall): Closing bridge in 30m after observability confirms stability. Thanks all. :rocket:
